entries.topic: Baptism in the Holy Spirit and tongues

approval.note: Approved as written. Levi, 'Approve all four'.

entries.perazimView: Spirit baptism is an experience distinct from conversion. Tongues are normal and desirable, but they are not the only evidence of Spirit baptism.

verses.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,
Have all the gifts of healing? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret?

otherViews: Classical Pentecostal view: Spirit baptism is a second experience after conversion, usually shown by speaking in tongues.
Cessationist view: the miraculous sign gifts, including tongues, ended with the apostolic age. The Spirit's work continues through regeneration and sanctification.
Many Christians hold views between these two, or hold that tongues may occur today without being required for every believer.

entries.topic: Prosperity teaching, giving and seed offerings

approval.note: Approved as written. Levi, 'Approve all four'.

entries.perazimView: God calls believers to generous, cheerful giving. God's blessing cannot be bought with a 'seed' or a pledge. Manipulation and pressure in giving are warned against. Tithing is UNDECIDED and is not taught here as a position.

verses.text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.
He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches, and he that giveth to the rich, shall surely come to want.
Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;

otherViews: Prosperity teaching holds that faith and giving bring material return as a rule. Critics say this turns God's gifts into a transaction and can burden poorer believers.
Some Christians hold that giving is an act of worship and trust, without a promised financial return.
Views on tithing differ widely. This topic does not settle that question.

entries.topic: Polygamy and families already in polygamous marriages

approval.note: Approved as written. Levi, 'Approve all four'.

entries.perazimView: Marriage is one man and one woman. Families already in polygamy receive pastoral care. They are not told to break up or abandon wives and children.

verses.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?
And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh.
A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach;
If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.

otherViews: Some interpreters read the polygamous households of the Old Testament as recorded, not endorsed. Others apply the 'husband of one wife' requirement for leaders (1 Timothy 3:2, Titus 1:6) more widely.
Christians differ on pastoral responses to existing polygamous marriages, especially where leaving a marriage would harm wives and children.

approval.note: Approved as written. Levi, 'Approve all four'.

entries.perazimView: Dowry is an acceptable custom when it honours both families. It must not become a sale of a person, a debt trap, or a reason to delay marriage.

verses.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.
Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD.

Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.

otherViews: Some see dowry as honouring both families and marking a covenant between them.
Others see a risk that dowry makes a person into a price, creates debt, or delays marriage. Local custom varies widely.
